doc.title: Network Troubleshooting Guide
doc.text:
# Network Troubleshooting Guide

## Packet Loss on Edge Routers
Intermittent packet loss on edge routers is most often caused by MTU mismatches between the overlay network and the physical uplink. The overlay adds a 50-byte VXLAN header, so the physical MTU must be at least 1550 when the overlay MTU is 1500.

## TLS Handshake Failures
A `handshake failure` alert usually means the client and server share no cipher suite, or the server certificate chain is incomplete. Verify the chain with `openssl s_client -connect host:443 -showcerts` and confirm the intermediate certificate is served.

## DNS Resolution Slowness
Slow DNS lookups inside pods are typically caused by the `ndots:5` default, which makes the resolver try every search domain before the absolute name. Set `ndots:2` in the pod DNS config for external-heavy workloads.

doc.title: Power and Cooling
doc.text:
# Power and Cooling

## Thermal Throttling
Servers throttle CPU frequency when inlet temperature exceeds 35°C. Sustained throttling shows up as unexplained latency spikes rather than errors. Check rack inlet sensors and confirm blanking panels are installed so hot exhaust air does not recirculate.

## PSU Redundancy Alerts
A `PSU redundancy lost` alert means one of the two power supplies has failed or lost input. The server keeps running on one PSU, but a second failure causes an immediate hard power-off. Replace the failed unit within the same maintenance window.

doc.title: Storage Node Runbook
doc.text:
# Storage Node Runbook

## Disk Errors

### SMART Failure Warnings
When a node reports `SMART overall-health self-assessment: FAILED`, the drive is predicting imminent failure. Drain the node with `omnictl node drain <node>` before replacing the disk. Do not reboot first: a reboot can turn a degraded drive into a dead one and force a full resync.

### I/O Timeouts (EIO-5)
Error code EIO-5 means the controller timed out waiting for a block write. Check the cable seating and the controller firmware version. Firmware below 4.2.1 has a known bug where queue depth above 64 triggers spurious timeouts; set `queue_depth=32` as a workaround.

## Replication Lag
If replication lag exceeds 30 seconds, the cluster marks the replica as stale. Common causes are a saturated 10GbE uplink or a replica stuck in compaction. Run `omnictl replica status` and look for `compaction=running`.

```bash
# This is a comment, not a heading
omnictl replica status --verbose
```

doc.title: Network Troubleshooting Guide
doc.text:
# Network Troubleshooting Guide

## Packet Loss on Edge Routers
Intermittent packet loss on edge routers is most often caused by MTU mismatches between the overlay network and the physical uplink. The overlay adds a 50-byte VXLAN header, so the physical MTU must be at least 1550 when the overlay MTU is 1500.

## TLS Handshake Failures
A `handshake failure` alert usually means the client and server share no cipher suite, or the server certificate chain is incomplete. Verify the chain with `openssl s_client -connect host:443 -showcerts` and confirm the intermediate certificate is served.

## DNS Resolution Slowness
Slow DNS lookups inside pods are typically caused by the `ndots:5` default, which makes the resolver try every search domain before the absolute name. Set `ndots:2` in the pod DNS config for external-heavy workloads.

doc.title: Power and Cooling
doc.text:
# Power and Cooling

## Thermal Throttling
Servers throttle CPU frequency when inlet temperature exceeds 35°C. Sustained throttling shows up as unexplained latency spikes rather than errors. Check rack inlet sensors and confirm blanking panels are installed so hot exhaust air does not recirculate.

## PSU Redundancy Alerts
A `PSU redundancy lost` alert means one of the two power supplies has failed or lost input. The server keeps running on one PSU, but a second failure causes an immediate hard power-off. Replace the failed unit within the same maintenance window.

doc.title: Storage Node Runbook
doc.text:
# Storage Node Runbook

## Disk Errors

### SMART Failure Warnings
When a node reports `SMART overall-health self-assessment: FAILED`, the drive is predicting imminent failure. Drain the node with `omnictl node drain <node>` before replacing the disk. Do not reboot first: a reboot can turn a degraded drive into a dead one and force a full resync.

### I/O Timeouts (EIO-5)
Error code EIO-5 means the controller timed out waiting for a block write. Check the cable seating and the controller firmware version. Firmware below 4.2.1 has a known bug where queue depth above 64 triggers spurious timeouts; set `queue_depth=32` as a workaround.

## Replication Lag
If replication lag exceeds 30 seconds, the cluster marks the replica as stale. Common causes are a saturated 10GbE uplink or a replica stuck in compaction. Run `omnictl replica status` and look for `compaction=running`.

```bash
# This is a comment, not a heading
omnictl replica status --verbose
```

doc.title: Network Troubleshooting Guide
doc.text:
# Network Troubleshooting Guide

## Packet Loss on Edge Routers
Intermittent packet loss on edge routers is most often caused by MTU mismatches between the overlay network and the physical uplink. The overlay adds a 50-byte VXLAN header, so the physical MTU must be at least 1550 when the overlay MTU is 1500.

## TLS Handshake Failures
A `handshake failure` alert usually means the client and server share no cipher suite, or the server certificate chain is incomplete. Verify the chain with `openssl s_client -connect host:443 -showcerts` and confirm the intermediate certificate is served.

## DNS Resolution Slowness
Slow DNS lookups inside pods are typically caused by the `ndots:5` default, which makes the resolver try every search domain before the absolute name. Set `ndots:2` in the pod DNS config for external-heavy workloads.

doc.text:
# Power and Cooling

## Thermal Throttling
Servers throttle CPU frequency when inlet temperature exceeds 35°C. Sustained throttling shows up as unexplained latency spikes rather than errors. Check rack inlet sensors and confirm blanking panels are installed so hot exhaust air does not recirculate.

## PSU Redundancy Alerts
A `PSU redundancy lost` alert means one of the two power supplies has failed or lost input. The server keeps running on one PSU, but a second failure causes an immediate hard power-off. Replace the failed unit within the same maintenance window.

doc.title: Storage Node Runbook
doc.text:
# Storage Node Runbook

## Disk Errors

### SMART Failure Warnings
When a node reports `SMART overall-health self-assessment: FAILED`, the drive is predicting imminent failure. Drain the node with `omnictl node drain <node>` before replacing the disk. Do not reboot first: a reboot can turn a degraded drive into a dead one and force a full resync.

### I/O Timeouts (EIO-5)
Error code EIO-5 means the controller timed out waiting for a block write. Check the cable seating and the controller firmware version. Firmware below 4.2.1 has a known bug where queue depth above 64 triggers spurious timeouts; set `queue_depth=32` as a workaround.

## Replication Lag
If replication lag exceeds 30 seconds, the cluster marks the replica as stale. Common causes are a saturated 10GbE uplink or a replica stuck in compaction. Run `omnictl replica status` and look for `compaction=running`.

```bash
# This is a comment, not a heading
omnictl replica status --verbose
```
